description: How the streaming scanner handles a <artifact> element. Its body goes to an artifact handler, not to the chat: the handler receives an open event, delta events carrying the body as it streams, then a close event with the whole body, and whatever it returns for the close event takes the element's place in the projected text. A malformed element, one whose body passes the cap, and one left open at the end of the stream are swallowed and reported as an error event instead. Output and events must not depend on where chunk boundaries fall, so a runner merges consecutive deltas for the same artifact before comparing and drops the deltas of an artifact that ends in an error (how much streamed before a failure depends on the chunking), and feeds each case the ways the citation_scan cases in citations.json are fed. '{{pad}}' expands to 'pad.char' repeated so the first artifact's body is exactly 'pad.artifact_body_length' characters, and '{{split}}' marks the case's own feed boundaries.

cases.name: an artifact streams its body and leaves the close handler's text
cases.why: The body never reaches the chat; the surrounding prose keeps its exact separators.
cases.text:
Here it is.

<artifact id="sales-report" title="Sales report">
---
title: Sales
---

Body.
</artifact>

Done.

cases.name: feed boundaries inside the tags do not change the result
cases.why: Partial open and close tags are held until they resolve.

cases.name: the title defaults to the id
cases.why: Every artifact needs a label for its chip and drawer.

cases.name: single quotes and unknown attributes are accepted
cases.why: Attribute order and quoting style are the model's choice; unknown names are ignored.

cases.name: tags match case-insensitively
cases.why: Matches how every other reserved element is found.

cases.name: an open tag mid-line is prose
cases.why: Like a citation, an artifact starts only at the beginning of a line, so a mention in a sentence is not one.

cases.name: a citation inside an artifact body is part of the body
cases.why: The body is a document, not chat prose, so nothing in it is projected.

cases.name: two artifacts in one response each get their events
cases.why: A response can create more than one artifact.

cases.name: a stray close tag is dropped
cases.why: Reserved markup never reaches the display.

cases.name: a longer element name is not an artifact
cases.why: Only the exact element name opens an artifact; the chip element passes through.

cases.name: a bare open tag has no id and is swallowed
cases.why: An id is required, so the element is malformed; its body is never shown.

cases.name: an id that is not a lowercase slug is malformed
cases.why: The id names a directory, so it is restricted to lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens.

cases.name: an unquoted attribute is malformed
cases.why: Only quoted attributes are part of the grammar.

cases.name: a header broken across lines is malformed
cases.why: The open tag sits on one line; a newline before '>' means it never closed.

cases.name: an artifact left open at the end of the stream is reported
cases.why: Incomplete documents are never committed; the handler hears why.

cases.name: a body at the cap is accepted
cases.why: The cap bounds what one response can stream into the drawer.

cases.name: a body past the cap is swallowed and reported
cases.why: What streamed before the cap was passed is abandoned with the rest.
